name: Lawn or Spontaneous Groundcover (photo ratings)
description: Faithful replication with the original photographs, for 4 of the paper's 13 ground covers: participants look at the three photographs of one ground cover, as each resident in the paper did, and rate it. The photographs show 2 m x 2 m test plots planted on one site in Xianyang, China, from two heights and angles (1.5 m parallel view, 1.5 m angled view) and a close-up at 0.3 m, in winter (December) and spring (March; the spring close-up combines four detail photos). The printed kinds are two spontaneous groundcovers, TCC (Taraxacum mongolicum - Cynodon dactylon - Conyza canadensis) and CVC (Coronilla varia - Veronica persica - Cynodon dactylon), and two lawns, O (Oxalis corymbosa) and FPL (Festuca elata - Poa pratensis - Lolium perenne). Each participant is randomly given one of the 8 sets (4 kinds x 2 seasons), sees its three photographs and, with them still shown, rates the paper's eight pairs of attributes (artificial/natural, domesticated/wild, boring/interesting, ugly/beautiful, neglected/well kept, monotonous/varied, non-ecological/ecological, with few species/with rich species) on 5-point scales (1 = very artificial, 2 = a little artificial, 3 = neutral, 4 = a little natural, 5 = very natural, and likewise for the other pairs) and answers the paper's preference question, How do you like these photos? (1 = very dislike, 5 = very like), with an optional reason. Gender, age group, education, occupation, monthly income, industry, living environment and attention to herbaceous plants are asked at the end. Rebuilt from Liang, Li, Xue, Liu, Jin, Wang, Gao, Chen, Li, Qiu & Gao (2023), Lawn or spontaneous groundcover? Residents' perceptions of and preferences for alternative lawns in Xianyang, China, Frontiers in Psychology 14: 1259920, with the photographs cropped from its Figure 2, the questions from its Methods and the background answer groups from its Supplementary Tables (CC BY 4.0). Image ids: kind_season_view, e.g. TCC_winter_1, FPL_spring_3; group records the set shown. Analysis as in the paper: t-test of spontaneous groundcovers against lawns and one-way ANOVA across kinds on each attribute and on preference, PCA of the eight attributes and regression of preference on the components, and generalized linear models of perception and preference by background; the paper (4,138 residents, face to face) found spontaneous groundcovers seen as more natural, wild, varied and species-rich and lawns as better kept, no overall difference in preference, TCC preferred most of all 13 kinds and significantly more than CVC and FPL, with O also scoring high among lawns. Differences from the original study: (1) only the 4 ground covers whose photographs are printed (Figure 2) are used, out of 13; (2) the photographs are shown on screen instead of printed at 297 x 180 mm in public spaces in Xianyang, and anyone can take part; (3) the paper gives the full labels only for artificial/natural and the end labels of the preference scale, so the labels of the other pairs and the middle preference points (2 = dislike, 3 = neutral, 4 = like) follow that example and are ours, as are the instruction texts; (4) the paper probed reasons in person; here an optional text box is used, its wording ours; (5) the background question wording is ours (the answer groups follow the paper's Supplementary Tables; the paper asked the attention question as Have you ever paid attention to the herbaceous plants around you in your everyday life?), and a prefer-not-to-say gender option is added; income groups are in yuan as in the paper.
author: Liang, Li, Xue, Liu, Jin, Wang, Gao, Chen, Li, Qiu & Gao
